content.value_statement: Unity ECS projects can become hard to structure, optimize, and explain. This skill provides DOTS patterns for components, systems, jobs, baking, command buffers, and Burst performance work.
actual_capabilities: Explains Unity ECS component, tag, buffer, and aspect patterns.
Shows how to structure ISystem and IJobEntity workflows.
Guides use of Entity Command Buffers for structural changes.
Covers baking GameObjects into entities with authoring components.
Provides performance guidance for Burst, jobs, queries, and native collections.
limitations: Does not run Unity Editor or validate projects directly.
Does not replace profiling with Unity Profiler or platform testing.
Focuses on Unity ECS and DOTS, not unrelated Unity workflows.
Examples require adaptation to the installed Unity Entities package version.

use_cases.title: Plan ECS Architecture
use_cases.description: Design components, systems, buffers, and aspects before implementing a data-oriented gameplay feature.

use_cases.title: Optimize Entity Updates
use_cases.description: Convert expensive update loops into Burst-friendly jobs and parallel ECS systems.

use_cases.title: Teach DOTS Patterns
use_cases.description: Create clear explanations for entity queries, command buffers, baking, and native collection lifecycles.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how Unity ECS components, systems, and entities should be separated for a simple movement feature.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an ECS architecture for enemy spawning with timers, prefabs, and command buffers. Include components and system responsibilities.

prompt_templates.title: Review Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my ECS update flow for Burst compatibility, parallel scheduling, structural changes, and native collection disposal risks.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate OOP Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration plan from MonoBehaviour enemy logic to Unity ECS using baking, aspects, jobs, and data-oriented state.

output_examples.input: Request: Design an ECS movement feature for many units.
output_examples.output: A structured plan with component data, movement system responsibilities, query strategy, Burst considerations, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Request: Improve a spawning system that creates entities during updates.
output_examples.output: Recommendations to use command buffers, schedule work safely, avoid hot-path structural changes, and verify behavior in profiling tools.

output_examples.input: Request: Explain why native collections must be disposed.
output_examples.output: A concise explanation of allocator lifetimes, cleanup timing, dependency handling, and common leak prevention practices.

best_practices: Profile first, then apply ECS, Jobs, and Burst changes to measured bottlenecks.
Keep component data small, explicit, and separated from behavior.
Use command buffers for structural changes and dispose native collections correctly.
anti_patterns: Do not put managed objects into Burst-critical component data.
Do not create or destroy entities directly inside parallel jobs.
Do not convert every small gameplay script to ECS without a performance reason.

faq.question: What Unity topics does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers ECS components, systems, jobs, Burst, command buffers, baking, aspects, queries, and native collection patterns.

faq.question: Can it debug my Unity project directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and review support, but it does not run Unity Editor or inspect scenes automatically.

faq.question: Is this useful for small games?
faq.answer: Yes, when a feature has many entities or CPU-bound logic. Simple scripts may not need ECS.

faq.question: Does it include performance advice?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Burst usage, job scheduling, structural changes, query choices, and native collection cleanup.

faq.question: Can it help migrate MonoBehaviour code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can outline components, authoring data, bakers, systems, and staged migration steps.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
